tools.name: describe_ui
tools.description: The app facts the app plugin reports for the live client: activeTab, the navigate targets (navTargets: the friendly names, and navTargetEntryPointIds: the entry-point ids), the toolbar's toolbarActions (id/label/enabled/submenu), the menu bar's leaf menuPaths, navEntryPoints (roots, children), the open view's viewTabs and sections (every section it registered, including one never built - 'created':false; target it by its 'id') with sectionProblems, the plugins' domain steps as 'vocabulary' sentences (id, kind, sentence; the vocabulary tool has their params), and any waiting dialog ('dialog': title, message, buttons - answer it with the 'answer' verb). Tables, buttons and fields are read from the element tree with 'snapshot' or 'read'. Pass 'fields' to get only the parts you need.

fields.description: Only these top-level fields, e.g. ["sections","dialog"] or ["activeTab","viewTabs"]; default all.

tools.name: do_action
tools.description: Execute ONE step against the live client and return pass/fail and its duration ('ms'). A step is a verb (click, type, press, ..., contextMenu) or one of the app steps navigate, close, loginAs. A successful step is recorded, unless it has no Java form (a loginAs after the first step, a target by ref): it runs but is not recorded, and 'notRecorded' says why. A do step is recorded even when its domain step has no Java form: export_recorded_test writes it, export_test refuses it. The 'action' object uses the step schema, e.g. {"action":"navigate","target":"home"} or {"action":"expect","target":{"role":"table"},"rows":{"op":"gte","value":1}}. A step that opens a message or confirmation returns at once with 'dialog' (title, message, buttons); navigate, close and loginAs refuse to run until it is answered with the 'answer' verb. A step may carry say: its sentence (one line, kept in the recording and the recorded test).

action.description: A step named by its 'action' field: a verb, navigate / close / loginAs, or do (a plugin's domain step: {"action":"do","step":<id>,"params":{<name>:<value as text>}}, which reports its filled sentence and the steps it ran, and is recorded as one step). The verbs are also tools of their own, with full argument schemas.

record.description: false keeps this step out of export_test's recording (used by tests)

_lease.description: lease token from session op 'lease'; omit while nobody holds the lease

tools.name: do_actions
tools.description: Execute SEVERAL steps in order against the live client, in one call, stopping at the first failure. Prefer this over repeated do_action when the next steps are already known. Returns {passed, ran, total, steps:[{passed, action, message}]}; successful steps are recorded for export_test exactly as do_action records them. Example: {"actions":[{"action":"navigate","target":"home"},{"action":"click","target":{"role":"tab","name":"Customer"}},{"action":"close"}]}. A step may carry say: its sentence.

items.description: A step named by its 'action' field: a verb, navigate / close / loginAs, or do (a plugin's domain step: {"action":"do","step":<id>,"params":{<name>:<value as text>}}, which reports its filled sentence and the steps it ran, and is recorded as one step). The verbs are also tools of their own, with full argument schemas.

_lease.description: lease token from session op 'lease'; omit while nobody holds the lease

tools.name: batch
tools.description: Run SEVERAL steps in ONE call, in order, stopping at the first that does not pass - use it whenever the next steps are already known. Each step runs, answers and records exactly as its own tool call would, so export_test writes the same test either way; 'read' steps record nothing, and a 'read' that finds nothing stops the batch. Returns {passed, ran, total, ms, steps:[{verb, passed, message, ms, recorded?, notRecorded?, ...}], snapshot?}. A harness error (CAPABILITY_GAP, INPUT_ERROR) is a tool error naming the step; the steps before it ran and were recorded. Example: {"steps":[{"verb":"click","target":{"role":"tab","name":"Customer"}},{"verb":"type","target":{"role":"text","name":"Name"},"text":"X"},{"verb":"expect","target":{"role":"button","name":"Save"},"state":["!disabled"]}]}.

steps.description: The steps, in order. Each is {"verb": <name>, ...the arguments that verb's own tool takes}.

verb.description: A verb tool's name (click, type, press, check, select, pick, menu, context_menu, answer, choose_file, drag, drop, expect, scroll, set_clipboard), 'read', or a step type (navigate, close, loginAs, screenshot, ...).

snapshot.description: true, or the snapshot tool's arguments (target, depth, compact, ...): a snapshot taken after the last step that ran, pass or fail.

_lease.description: lease token from session op 'lease'; omit while nobody holds the lease

tools.name: export_test
tools.description: Write the steps recorded since the last session reset as a JUnit @UiTest class under <module>/src/test/java/<package>/<class>.java (the module is the app plugin's export module, else the working directory; -Dswingui.testsDir overrides). The test starts where the recording did, right after a reset, so it must begin by getting to its own starting screen: without an app plugin a reset only closes dialogs, and startWarning flags a test that does not begin with menu, press or navigate. Only steps with a Java form are recorded (verbs, including expect for checks; navigate, close, a leading loginAs; do steps), except a do step whose domain step has no Java form: a recording with one is refused, naming it - export it with export_recorded_test instead. Refuses a recording that did not begin at a reset or a recording start, a bad class/method/package name, an existing file, or an empty recording, naming each problem; a refusal keeps the recording. A step and its checks are one block; sentences become comments.

class.description: Test class name; must end in UiIT, e.g. PlaceOrderUiIT

package.description: Java package (default: the app plugin's export package, else 'recorded')

clear.description: Empty the recording after exporting (default: true); reset before recording the next test. Refused while a recording started by recording start or the person's Record runs: export with clear false, or stop it first

_lease.description: lease token from session op 'lease'; omit while nobody holds the lease

tools.name: export_recorded_test
tools.description: Write the steps recorded since the last session reset as a recorded test file <recorded tests folder>/<name>.json: UI steps and checks of what is visible, no compiling; run it with run_recorded_test, from the palette, or in Maven with the JUnit runner (RecordedTests). Same rules as export_test: it must have begun at a reset or a recording start, startWarning flags a recorded test that does not begin with menu, press or navigate, an empty recording or a bad name is refused, and an existing file is never overwritten - except the recorded test the recording came from (loaded in the palette, or exported before without clear). A folder that cannot be written is refused, naming it. A recorded test holds exact values: check data the test creates or data known to exist; a value the app makes up (a new order number, today's date) only when your start makes it predictable - otherwise check something else or write a Java test. Format version 2 (3 when it holds do steps, with requires naming their plugins): each step with its checks nested, sentences and groups kept.

name.description: The file name without .json, e.g. place-order

dir.description: The folder; default the recorded tests folder: agent option recorded=, else -Dswingui.recordedDir, else uitest in the app's working directory

description.description: What the recorded test does, one sentence

clear.description: Empty the recording after exporting (default: true); reset before recording the next recorded test. Refused while a recording started by recording start or the person's Record runs: export with clear false, or stop it first

_lease.description: lease token from session op 'lease'; omit while nobody holds the lease

tools.name: run_recorded_test
tools.description: Run a recorded test file on the live app and report it: one of 'name' (in the recorded tests folder), 'path', or 'test' (the file's JSON inline). It begins as every recorded test does, with a reset (dialogs closed; with an app plugin its reset), runs every step as do_action would WITHOUT recording, and stops at the first that fails; that step carries what its locators match now, a scoped tree and a picture of the window (written under 'evidence', default target/ui-screenshots/failures). Returns {passed, ran, total, steps, report}; ran and total count steps, each entry of steps is a step or a check: [{n, say?, action, passed, ms, message?, reason?, details?, warning?, diagnostics?}], n a step number (7) or a check label ("7.2"); action is the step's technical line. After a failure take a new snapshot before using refs. Refused (BUSY) while a person records, answers or replays in the palette. From a shell the CLI exits 4 when the recorded test fails.

name.description: A recorded test in the recorded tests folder, without .json, e.g. place-order

path.description: A recorded test file, absolute or relative to the app's working directory

test.description: The recorded test file's JSON inline (what export_recorded_test writes)

evidence.description: The folder for the failing step's picture; default target/ui-screenshots/failures

_lease.description: lease token from session op 'lease'; omit while nobody holds the lease

tools.name: snapshot
tools.description: The live client as an element tree: every showing window, dialog and popup (focused window first, popups last), each element with role, name, value, state and a ref (e1, e2, ...). Refs stay valid until the next snapshot; pass one as {"ref":"e12"} as a verb's target. SCOPE IT: an unscoped snapshot is the whole app and costs thousands of tokens. Give a 'target' locator (e.g. {"scope":["tab:Customer"],"role":"section","name":"Header"} or {"role":"tab","name":"Line items"}) for one element's subtree, 'depth' for a few levels, and compact:true to drop rows and items. The answer ends with 'size' {nodes, bytes, scoped}.

window.description: Only the roots this names: main | popup | dialog | dialog:<title> | window:<title>

ref.description: Only this element's subtree (a ref from the previous snapshot)

target.description: Only this element's subtree, found like a verb's target - a tab's content for a tab. At most one of window, ref and target.

scope.description: Ordered tab:<title> / section:<caption> steps the element sits in (a section is any titled border, even one on a clickable box); a title or caption ending in * matches a prefix (tab:New order*); an id:<name> step means strictly inside the component whose getName() is <name> (not a contributed section id).

row.description: Table row: {"<column header>": "<cell text>", ...} or {"index": n}.

nth.description: Which match, in tree order, when the locator is not unique (makes the step fragile).

A node carries 'tooltip' when the element (or the rendered cell) shows one. A target that does not resolve returns found:false with candidates.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: A PNG of the app: the target element, or the current window when no target is given. It PAINTS the app's own components into an offscreen image - it never grabs the screen - so it captures the client whether or not it is in front, takes no focus, and cannot catch another application's window. Give a 'target' for one dialog, panel, table or toolbar, and 'region' for a snippet inside it. Anything drawn in a window of its own (an open popup menu, a combo dropdown, a tooltip) is NOT in the image - capture that window instead. The person's palette and any boxes shown in the app are not in the image. 'palette': true keeps the palette, the boxes and the open menus in the picture, as the person sees the window (for documentation); default false. A read: nothing is recorded; to capture screens in a recorded test, use the 'screenshot' step in a batch, which writes a file. Use it for an aesthetic call - alignment, cropping, overlap, proportion - and an 'expect' for anything that is really a number or a boolean.

tools.name: recording
tools.description: The recording the agent and the person at the app make together (works with the palette on or off). start {reset?}: a fresh recording; with the palette on the person's steps join it and the palette shows it; reset:true resets the app first, as a test starts. stop: ends it (the person's Done does too); after it no step joins. Steps are numbered 1..n; a step is an action and the checks after it, numbered n.k (7.2); checks before any action are step 1. list {wait?}: state, who started it, rev, and every step with n, author (person, agent, loaded), line, java, its step JSON, say, edited (changed and not replayed since), group (its number in groups) and its checks nested under it ({n: "7.1", ...}), plus groups [{from, to, say}] in step numbers; a check-only step 1 has no line, step or java; wait (ms) waits until it stops (not for a session reset's). insert {at, step}: an action at a step number (before the step now there) or a check at a label ("7.2"), NOT run (marked edited until a replay passes it); nothing can go in front of a check-only step 1. delete {n | from, to}: a step goes with its checks, "7.2" only that check. move {n, to}: a step with its checks (a check is deleted and inserted again). edit {n, target | text | step | say}: n is a step or a check; say sets its sentence (one line, "" removes it) and may come with target, text or step. group {from, to, say}: steps from..to (two or more, whole steps, groups do not nest or overlap) under one sentence; the same range renames it. ungroup {n}: ends the group that holds step n, its steps stay. row {n, by}: a step or check on a table row names it by value (the key column's text: it still finds the row after a sort or a new row) or by position (its index); list shows each one's row {by, value, index}; the other way is known once the step ran (a loaded step: after one passing replay); an edit like the others. undo: takes back the last edit, by you or the person. Numbers close up after a delete; deleting or moving a step takes its checks along; pass rev from your last list so an edit is refused if the person changed the recording meanwhile. Every edit returns the new list. While one runs, session reset and test runs are refused; stop it first. replay {from?, to?, speed?}: runs the steps (with their checks) again without recording them and returns {passed, ran, total, reset, steps}: ran and total count steps, with one {n, action, passed, ms, message?} entry per step or check run (n as in list; action is its technical line); from step 1 it resets the app first, as the exported test starts. redo {from}: cuts step from and the ones after it, replays the steps before it from a reset, and records on (from = the number after the last step continues a stopped recording). export {as: recorded|java, ...}: as export_recorded_test / export_test, but keeps the recording. load {name | path}: a recorded test file becomes the recording (stopped; redo or insert to add to it).

at.description: insert: where it goes. An action: the step number it gets (1 to steps+1), before the step now there. A check: the label it gets, a step number and its place under it ("7.2"; k up to the step's checks + 1), or 1 for a check-only step 1. A step number (7) or a check label ("7.2").

n.description: delete, move, edit, ungroup, row: a step number (7) or a check label ("7.2"). delete 7 deletes the step and its checks, delete "7.2" only that check; move takes a step (with its checks); edit "7.2" edits that check; ungroup takes any step of the group.

from.description: delete, group: first step of a range; replay: first step (default 1); redo: the step to record again (steps+1 continues).

speed.description: replay: pauses for a person watching.

say.description: edit: the step's or check's sentence, one line of at most 200 characters ("" removes it), alone or with target, text or step; group: the group's sentence.

by.description: row: how the table row of step or check n is named: value (its key column's text, as recorded when a column told the rows apart) or position (its index).

step.description: insert, edit: a step or check as do_action takes it.

tools.name: scroll
tools.description: Scrolls a table, tree, list or panel: to an end with 'to', by whole screens with 'pages', or until a row is in view by giving the target a 'row'. Exactly one of the three. tools.name: session
tools.description: The agent itself. info (default): versions, app start, lease, plugins (the plugins array lists every plugin with its state). lease {owner, ttlMs}: take the agent for one owner; pass the token as _lease on every mutating call. release {token}. renew {token}: keep the lease alive while the test makes no call; answers renewed: false once the lease is gone. reset {alias | user+password}: the start of every test: close modal dialogs; with an app plugin also its reset (tabs, login as alias or user). Starts a fresh recording for export_test; refused while a recording runs (recording start or ● Record): recording stop or Done ends it. login {alias | user+password | relogin:true}: switch users mid-test. edt: the client's event-thread stack.
